messages:
marta: heads up — perf-ci-bot flagged a microbench regression on PR #8899. 
perf-ci-bot: CI microbench: model=llama-7b seq=512 iters=200 — median token latency +18% (threshold diff exceeded). details: https://ci.internal/perf/8899/diff (artifacts attached) :warning:
perf-ci-bot: regression trace: kernel_autoselect_path increased. suspect: kernel selection heuristics change in recent merges.
sam: ugh. which merge landed in that PR? any obvious diffs in kernel selector?
marta: PR touches kernel_selector.rs and batching/heuristics.py — small reorder of heuristics (changed boundary from 128 -> 256).
lee: I pulled the CI artifact and ran the microbench locally: `./scripts/run_microbench --model llama-7b --seq 512 --iters 200`
lee: local result: baseline (main): median token latency 14.2ms, PR head: 16.8ms. p95 went 22.5ms -> 28.1ms. reproduces cleanly.
kai: can you paste the diff that changed the threshold? thought we intentionally tuned to 128 to favor fused kernel on short seqs.
marta: snippet from PR: ```diff
- if avg_seq_len < 128:
-     select(fused_attention)
+ if avg_seq_len < 256:
+     select(fused_attention)
```
lee: that change forces the fused kernel path for more requests, but on our tiled kernel the throughput for longer seqs + batch combos was better due to KV layout. the fused path has higher per-token overhead for seq>256 in practice — explains the spike.
sam: let's bisect to confirm which merge introduced the behavioral change. I'll run a git-bisect between main@{1 week} and HEAD of the PR. expect the offending commit is the one that adjusted the 128->256 heuristic.
perf-ci-bot: bisect job started by sam — results will be posted here.
sam: bisect finished — culprit commit = abc1234 (author: dylan) titled "tune kernel autoselect boundary". reproduces locally when checking out that commit.
kai: quick profiler (perf top) on the PR head shows top hotspots: select_kernel() 34%, compute_attention() 26%, kv_cache_lookup() 8%. select_kernel increased a lot due to additional runtime checks.
marta: minimal mitigation options: revert the heuristic change (quick), or adjust boundary to 192 and add a microbench unit test to lock it in. reverting is fastest for rollout blocker.
sam: I'll open a revert PR now (cc @dylan). also adding a failing golden to the microbench CI so future changes fail fast.
lee: after revert candidate locally, run shows median 14.3ms again. good.
kai: follow-up: create a perf test that runs seq distribution [32,128,512] and asserts kernel selection counts, and add telemetry so runtime reports which kernel chosen per-request to console for debugging.
marta: thanks — action items: sam -> revert PR, sam -> add CI golden; kai -> perf test + telemetry; lee -> quick note in changelog. marking this rollout-blocker until revert merges. :white_check_mark:
